newsitem.title: CANADA: Snow, cold likely ends Canada Prairie harvest.
newsitem.headline: Snow, cold likely ends Canada Prairie harvest.

text.p: Cold weather and heavy snow ended Canada's Prairie harvest with some crops likely to remain in the field until the spring, Pioneer Grain Co Ltd said in its last crop report for the week ended Oct 30.
British Columbia's Dawson Creek and Alberta's Peace River Valley harvest progressed quickly in the last week with some farmers harvesting on frost. Up to 60 percent of the harvest was done.
Alberta farmers had harvested 100 percent of flax, 97 percent of barley, 96 percent of wheat, 95 percent of durum and canola, 93 percent of oats and 90 percent of rye.
The balance will likely be left in the field until spring. Overall crop quality was below average.

Harvest of Saskatchewan's northern grainbelt was near complete in the west and central areas with 95 percent of crops in the bin. The balance will likely be left in the field until the spring. The east wrapped up harvest with about 90 of crops combined. Crop quality region-wide was below average.

Southwest Saskatchewan harvested 95 percent of its crops. Weather makes it unlikely the remainder will be harvested before spring. Quality seemed a bit below average with 60 percent of wheat, durum wheat and flax expected to grade No1.
Up to 80 percent of canola and barley may grade as No1.

Southeast Saskatchewan harvested 90 to 95 percent of crops with the balance likely to be harvested next spring. Crop quality was affected by the recent cool, wet weather. Ninety five percent of flax and canola, 80 percent of barley, 40 percent of wheat and oats and 30 percent of durum wheat were expected to grade as No1.
Eastern Saskatchewan and Manitoba harvested virtually all fields. Crop quality appeared to be average for most crops.
